source.author: verg
source.text: At rex sollicitus monstris oracula Fauni, fatidici; genitoris, adit lucosque sub alta consulit Albunea, nemorum quae maxima sacro fonte sonat saevamque exhalat opaca mephitim.
source.text_original: At rex sollicitus monstris oracula Fauni, / fatidici; genitoris, adit lucosque sub alta / consulit Albunea, nemorum quae maxima sacro / fonte sonat saevamque exhalat opaca mephitim.
source.text_english: But the king, troubled by the prodigies, seeks the oracles of Faunus, the prophet, his father’s; he approaches the groves beneath lofty Albunea and consults her, who, greatest of the woodlands, sounds with her holy spring and breathes out in the shade a savage vapour.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Prima deum magnis canimus freta pervia natis fatidicamque ratem, Scythici quae Phasidis oras ausa sequi mediosque inter iuga concita cursus rumpere flammifero tandem consedit Olympo.
reuse.text_original: Prima deum magnis canimus freta pervia natis / fatidicamque ratem, Scythici quae Phasidis oras / ausa sequi mediosque inter iuga concita cursus / rumpere flammifero tandem consedit Olympo.
reuse.text_english: First we sing of the sea passages made traversable by the great sons of the gods, and of the prophetic ship, which, daring to follow the Scythian shores of Phasis and, driven on, to break through its course amid the middle mountain ridges, at last settled on fiery Olympus.
